evidence.claim: In his national address, Tshisekedi said he was choosing diplomacy over war, cited the East African Community and Luanda processes, and described the eastern crisis as having displaced more than 200,000 people.
evidence.title: Adresse à la nation du Président de la République, Félix Tshisekedi suite à la détérioration de la situation sécuritaire à l’est du pays
evidence.excerpt: In his national address, Tshisekedi said he was choosing diplomacy over war, cited the East African Community and Luanda processes, and described the eastern crisis as having displaced more than 200,000 people.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct presidential statement with explicit crisis-management choices and dates.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly Tshisekedi's own crisis framing and choice set.
contrary_evidence: This concerns conventional-security de-escalation, not nuclear command or arsenal decisions.

evidence.claim: EAC leaders agreed to send a regional force to the DRC, called for an immediate ceasefire, and said the force would work with DRC military and administrative authorities to stabilise the east.
evidence.title: East Africa leaders agree regional force to quell DR Congo crisis
evidence.excerpt: EAC leaders agreed to send a regional force to the DRC, called for an immediate ceasefire, and said the force would work with DRC military and administrative authorities to stabilise the east.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters-sourced regional diplomacy report with explicit meeting outcomes.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Tshisekedi was a direct participant in the summit, but the decision was regional rather than unilateral.
contrary_evidence: This is diplomacy around an inherited conflict, not proof of durable implementation.

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that Tshisekedi and Kagame were due to begin talks in Luanda amid the M23 offensive, and that Tshisekedi arrived for a mini tripartite summit on peace.
evidence.title: Congo and Rwanda to begin talks amid tensions over insurgency
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that Tshisekedi and Kagame were due to begin talks in Luanda amid the M23 offensive, and that Tshisekedi arrived for a mini tripartite summit on peace.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters wire content reproduced by Euronews with named leaders, date, and meeting purpose.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Tshisekedi's diplomatic conduct and participation.
contrary_evidence: Talks were held amid escalation, so the source does not show success or restraint alone.

evidence.claim: The CEEAC summit called for the immediate withdrawal of M23 in line with the Nairobi roadmap, and the report notes that Tshisekedi opened the conference in Kinshasa under a heightened security context.
evidence.title: Tension RDC-Rwanda : la CEEAC exige le retrait du M23
evidence.excerpt: The CEEAC summit called for the immediate withdrawal of M23 in line with the Nairobi roadmap, and the report notes that Tshisekedi opened the conference in Kinshasa under a heightened security context.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous local-language political reporting on regional diplomacy and Tshisekedi's role as host and president in office.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly about Tshisekedi's hosting and political positioning.
contrary_evidence: The item reflects regional pressure, not a unilateral Congolese initiative.

evidence.claim: The presidency said Uhuru Kenyatta was visiting Kinshasa as EAC facilitator for the Nairobi peace process and that the talks were preparing the third round of peace negotiations with armed groups willing to disarm.
evidence.title: Le président Félix Tshisekedi a reçu l'ancien président kenyan, Uhuru Kenyatta
evidence.excerpt: The presidency said Uhuru Kenyatta was visiting Kinshasa as EAC facilitator for the Nairobi peace process and that the talks were preparing the third round of peace negotiations with armed groups willing to disarm.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary presidential communication on an actual meeting and peace-process preparation.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Tshisekedi's engagement with the Nairobi process.
contrary_evidence: Official favorable framing; it does not prove battlefield results.

evidence.claim: The Luanda mini-summit produced a ceasefire to take effect on 25 November and required M23 to withdraw from occupied areas in the DRC.
evidence.title: Le mini-sommet de Luanda impose au m23/Rwanda un cessez-le-feu et le retrait des zones occupées en RDC
evidence.excerpt: The Luanda mini-summit produced a ceasefire to take effect on 25 November and required M23 to withdraw from occupied areas in the DRC.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary presidency communiqué on a dated regional agreement in which Tshisekedi participated.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly tied to Tshisekedi's participation in a regional settlement effort.
contrary_evidence: Agreement terms do not establish compliance or long-term peace.

evidence.claim: Tshisekedi said M23 had to stop hostilities, withdraw from its positions, and return to its November 2021 lines as a condition for joining the Nairobi peace process.
evidence.title: Troisième phase des pourparlers de Nairobi : Les chefs d’Etats appellent les groupes armés à déposer les armes
evidence.excerpt: Tshisekedi said M23 had to stop hostilities, withdraw from its positions, and return to its November 2021 lines as a condition for joining the Nairobi peace process.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct quotation of Tshisekedi in contemporaneous local-language reporting on the Nairobi process.
evidence.period_fit: Exact 2022 ruler statement during peace negotiations
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly Tshisekedi's own public peace-process position.
contrary_evidence: This is a stated condition for talks, not proof that the condition was enforceable.

evidence.claim: The ICRC said clashes in Rutshuru had forced more than 72,000 people to flee in one week and urged all combatants to protect civilians and allow humanitarian workers access.
evidence.title: In eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), the surge in violence has driven thousands of displaced people to the outskirts of Goma
evidence.excerpt: The ICRC said clashes in Rutshuru had forced more than 72,000 people to flee in one week and urged all combatants to protect civilians and allow humanitarian workers access.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary humanitarian field report from the ICRC with exact displacement figures and IHL framing.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Conflict context under Tshisekedi, with implications for state protection duties.
contrary_evidence: This is field reporting on armed clashes, not a finding of presidential culpability.

evidence.claim: UNHCR reported over 800 deaths from firearm and machete attacks in Ituri between February and June 2022, including many people sheltering in displacement sites, and said recent fighting in North Kivu had displaced more than 160,000 people.
evidence.title: UNHCR gravely concerned by death toll of displaced in DR Congo's east
evidence.excerpt: UNHCR reported over 800 deaths from firearm and machete attacks in Ituri between February and June 2022, including many people sheltering in displacement sites, and said recent fighting in North Kivu had displaced more than 160,000 people.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Authoritative humanitarian briefing with concrete casualty and displacement figures.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect inherited-conflict context for Tshisekedi's security decisions.
contrary_evidence: It does not itself separate rebel, local, or government responsibility for each death.

evidence.claim: UNICEF said armed attacks in Rutshuru killed four children and that more than 158,000 people, about half children, had been displaced since late March in Rutshuru and Nyiragongo.
evidence.title: Les enfants sous attaque dans l'escalade du conflit à l'est de la RDC
evidence.excerpt: UNICEF said armed attacks in Rutshuru killed four children and that more than 158,000 people, about half children, had been displaced since late March in Rutshuru and Nyiragongo.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary UNICEF country office press release with exact date and displacement figures.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirect civilian-harm context under Tshisekedi's government.
contrary_evidence: This does not assign the attacks to Tshisekedi personally.

evidence.claim: UNICEF said humanitarian access was becoming more restricted because of the deteriorating security situation, and that fighting between Congolese forces and M23 had intensified since 20 October 2022.
evidence.title: UNICEF: Mass displacements in eastern DRC pose a deadly threat to children and young people
evidence.excerpt: UNICEF said humanitarian access was becoming more restricted because of the deteriorating security situation, and that fighting between Congolese forces and M23 had intensified since 20 October 2022.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary UNICEF briefing with a dated statement about access constraints and escalation.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Relevant to Tshisekedi's ability to protect civilians and sustain access.
contrary_evidence: A humanitarian access warning is not a direct finding of commander-level negligence.

evidence.claim: UNICEF reported that the latest wave of violence had driven 190,000 people from their homes and that many children arrived alone or separated from their families at displacement sites.
evidence.title: Facing displacement alone
evidence.excerpt: UNICEF reported that the latest wave of violence had driven 190,000 people from their homes and that many children arrived alone or separated from their families at displacement sites.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary UNICEF field story with a concrete displacement estimate and protection consequence.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirectly relevant to the government's civilian-protection record.
contrary_evidence: Story format is illustrative rather than a full incident ledger.

evidence.claim: UNICEF described a displaced mother in North Kivu who fled armed conflict and said she lost her husband and agricultural harvest, illustrating the conflict's destructive effect on livelihoods and schooling.
evidence.title: Life is tough here
evidence.excerpt: UNICEF described a displaced mother in North Kivu who fled armed conflict and said she lost her husband and agricultural harvest, illustrating the conflict's destructive effect on livelihoods and schooling.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary field story, but anecdotal rather than statistical.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Context for the social cost of the eastern conflict under Tshisekedi.
contrary_evidence: A single vignette cannot establish national-level responsibility on its own.

evidence.claim: Human Rights Watch said M23 summarily killed at least 29 civilians since mid-June 2022 and expanded control in the east, documenting deliberate civilian harm by the rebels.
evidence.title: DR Congo: Resurgent M23 Rebels Target Civilians
evidence.excerpt: Human Rights Watch said M23 summarily killed at least 29 civilians since mid-June 2022 and expanded control in the east, documenting deliberate civilian harm by the rebels.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Well-documented independent human-rights report based on field reporting and interviews.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirectly relevant to Tshisekedi's security environment and proxy-control problem.
contrary_evidence: The source is about M23 conduct, not direct acts by Tshisekedi.

evidence.claim: The article reported that the renewed M23 fighting had again displaced tens of thousands, with by the end of May 72,000 displaced according to the UN, and described the reappearance of old patterns of violence in North Kivu.
evidence.title: It shouldn’t be happening again: M23 rebels return to wreak havoc in DRC
evidence.excerpt: The article reported that the renewed M23 fighting had again displaced tens of thousands, with by the end of May 72,000 displaced according to the UN, and described the reappearance of old patterns of violence in North Kivu.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent field reporting with a clear date and referenced UN displacement estimate.
contrary_evidence: This is descriptive context, not a direct attribution of policy choice.

evidence.claim: The article said since November 2021 the M23 fighting had killed hundreds and forced nearly 200,000 people from their homes and land, separating families across Rutshuru.
evidence.title: I prayed to God to find him: the families scattered by violence in DRC
evidence.excerpt: The article said since November 2021 the M23 fighting had killed hundreds and forced nearly 200,000 people from their homes and land, separating families across Rutshuru.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent reporting with a direct displacement estimate and year-specific conflict timeline.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Context for Tshisekedi's conflict-handling choices and civilian-protection record.
contrary_evidence: It is reportorial context, not a legal or official finding.

evidence.claim: AP reported that UN experts had solid evidence that members of Rwanda's armed forces were operating in eastern Congo in support of M23, which was driving deaths and massive civilian displacement.
evidence.title: UN experts: Rwandan forces operate with M23 rebels in Congo
evidence.excerpt: AP reported that UN experts had solid evidence that members of Rwanda's armed forces were operating in eastern Congo in support of M23, which was driving deaths and massive civilian displacement.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: AP wire report summarizing a confidential UN expert finding with precise attribution and consequences.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Indirectly relevant to Tshisekedi's conflict environment and claims about external support.
contrary_evidence: This does not prove Tshisekedi's own conduct; it supports the external-aggression context.

evidence.claim: At the UN General Assembly, Tshisekedi said Rwanda's involvement and responsibility in the tragedy in areas occupied by the Rwandan army and its M23 allies were no longer questionable.
evidence.title: Congo crisis in focus at UN General Assembly
evidence.excerpt: At the UN General Assembly, Tshisekedi said Rwanda's involvement and responsibility in the tragedy in areas occupied by the Rwandan army and its M23 allies were no longer questionable.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Independent reporting of a ruler statement at a dated multilateral forum.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly Tshisekedi's public narrative about the conflict.
contrary_evidence: This records Tshisekedi's accusation, not independent proof that the accusation was fully correct.

evidence.claim: The presidency said Tshisekedi issued ordinances reshuffling the FARDC command, including naming Christian Tshiwewe as chief of staff, as part of military reform.
evidence.title: Profonds changements au commandement de l'armée : Tshiwewe a l'état-major général Fardc et Ephraïm Kabi à la garde républicaine
evidence.excerpt: The presidency said Tshisekedi issued ordinances reshuffling the FARDC command, including naming Christian Tshiwewe as chief of staff, as part of military reform.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary announcement of personnel changes in the armed forces made under presidential authority.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Tshisekedi's formal authority over military appointments.
contrary_evidence: A personnel reshuffle does not by itself show better battlefield performance or accountability.

unresolved_gaps: No direct 2022 nuclear/existential-risk decision by Tshisekedi is evidenced, and the package never shows operational nuclear control, brinkmanship, or safeguard intervention.
Direct 2022 execution and household/distribution outcome evidence remains thinner than the policy and macro coverage.
Direct, nationally representative 2022 welfare-outcome evidence attributable to Tshisekedi remains limited relative to the amount of partner-led program evidence.

Direct personal-nexus evidence is still sparse: no clear 2022 asset-declaration, campaign-finance, beneficial-ownership, or court/audit record ties Tshisekedi himself to self-dealing or deliberate deception.
Independent, audited delivery and outcome evidence is thinner than the program rhetoric and internal reporting.
